adjudication_label: batch_2:Simulation methodology comparison: annealing protocols vs MC/MD
canonical_question: Would the annealing protocol used by Wu et al. (above 2000 K followed by cooling) produce different SRO patterns than the MC/MD method used by Huang et al.?

question_variants.question: Would the annealing protocol used by Wu et al. (above 2000 K followed by cooling) produce different SRO patterns than the MC/MD method used by Huang et al.?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence describes the annealing protocol used by Wu et al. (CTIP, >2000 K cooling) but does not provide the specific SRO patterns resulting from this protocol, nor does it detail the MC/MD method used by Huang et al. in sufficient detail to compare the resulting SRO patterns directly.

answers.answer: The text mentions the method used by Wu et al. involved a charge-transfer ionic potential (CTIP) optimized with machine learning to anneal a sample above 2000 K and then cool down to room temperature, but does not provide the resulting SRO patterns or compare them to Huang et al.'s MC/MD method.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative SRO pattern data provided for Wu et al. vs Huang et al.
evidence_spans: We study the effects of the chemical short-range order (SRO) on the thermal conductivity of the refractory high-entropy alloy HfNbTaTiZr using atomistic simulation.
Samples with different degrees of chemical SRO are prepared by a Monte Carlo scheme.
With increasing SRO, a tendency of forming HfTi and TiZr clusters is found.
